subject: Swanlake AI - regional dedicated pool proposal & SOW next steps
messages:
From: Ethan Rivera <ethan.rivera@swanlake.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@swanlake.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity request - US + APAC (pilot)

Hi Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost numbers look promising. Swanlake is starting a paid pilot and we need a proposal for dedicated capacity in two regions (US-West + Singapore) to support an initial launch (Q3). High-level asks below: 

- Support ~120 RPS steady state across both regions with 2x burst to 240 RPS for 10 minute windows
- Typical input sequence length ~512 tokens; occasional spikes to 1024 tokens
- P99 latency target: <=200ms for token generation across our main endpoint (chat-like assistant)
- Timeline: pilot start Aug 1; 6 month initial commitment likely

Can you share a sizing proposal (GPUs, pool layout, fallback strategy), estimated costs for a 6-month reserved commitment, and any constraints we should be aware of? Procurement is on copy — they’ll need an SOW and preliminary pricing.

Attaching our internal capacity intake form to keep things structured.

Thanks,
Ethan Rivera
Head of Product, Swanlake AI
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Rivera <ethan.rivera@swanlake.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request - US + APAC (pilot)

Hi Ethan — looping in infra and capacity planning (Karthik, Soojin, Ben).

Quick summary of next steps from Redwood:

1) We’ll map three sizing tiers (small / medium / large) to help you pick risk vs cost for the pilot. Each tier includes dedicated pools in US-West and SG with a regional failover lane in EU for cross-region resilience.

2) We need two traffic artifacts from you to finalize sizing: per-endpoint RPS distribution (1h sample) and token-length histogram. The intake form you attached is perfect — I filled the first page and attached our preliminary cost model for a 6-mo reserved baseline.

3) Technical ask: confirm whether you’ll require on-prem KMS integration or we can use Redwood-managed keys for the pilot. Procurement should confirm CISO needs.

I attached: swanlake_capacity_request_form.xlsx (filled), preliminary_cost_model.csv (estimates).

Tentative timeline for Redwood deliverables:
- 48 hours: sizing options & cost ranges
- 5 business days: draft SOW and mutual action plan link

If that works, I’ll prepare the draft SOW and a recommended pool mapping for Karthik.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Rivera <ethan.rivera@swanlake.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@swanlake.ai, Arun Patel <arun.patel@swanlake.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 02:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request - US + APAC (pilot)

Marissa — thanks, attached is the RPS sample and token histogram (swanlake_traffic_profiles.pdf). A few follow-ups: 

- Can Redwood guarantee P99 <=200ms for the pilot under the committed baseline? If not, what mitigations can meet our UX target?
- For cost planning, can you provide a comparison between fully dedicated pools vs a hybrid (dedicated baseline + hostable burst on shared fleet)?

Procurement: we’ll need an SOW and a redline-ready contract skeleton to start internal review.

—Ethan

> Attachment: swanlake_traffic_profiles.pdf (3 pages)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Swanlake sizing — draft mapping and internal ask

Marissa / Team — reviewing the traffic file Ethan sent. Early mapping / assumptions: 

- Baseline sustained load: 120 RPS across two regions (assume split 70% US / 30% APAC based on profile)
- Effective token distribution: median 420, p95 ~780, p99 ~980
- Target SLO: aim for p99 <= 200ms with 95th percentile of requests served on dedicated pool (avoid hitting shared fallback often)

Draft capacity recommendation (conservative):
- US-West dedicated pool: 8 x A100-80GB equiv (quantization-enabled serving for seq<=512)
- SG dedicated edge pool: 4 x A100-80GB equiv with local KV caching to reduce cross-region fetches
- EU standby lane (warm): 2 x A100-80GB equiv (failover + can be used for sharded batch reruns)

Operational asks / risks:
- Burst handling: propose dedicated baseline with autoscale headroom plus configured burst to shared fleet (hybrid) for extreme tails. Hybrid lowers cost but increases variability in p99.
- Quantization profile: recommend int8 path for the medium tier to reduce GPU footprint; will validate quality against Swanlake eval set.

Approval request: Marissa — ok to offer a 6-month trial price at ~20% below list for SWAN-1973 to accelerate sign? If approved, I’ll produce redlines in the draft SOW and reserve APAC nodes in our capacity plan.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Swanlake sizing — draft mapping and internal ask

Quick tuning notes and a concrete pool plan (see attached):

- US-West (8 x A100 equiv): maps to 4 serving shards with hot-key KV caching; expected sustained throughput ~140 RPS with headroom for bursts to 280 RPS for short windows. Estimate p99 token-gen ~160-190ms when quantization path used and batching tuned for 50ms tail-latency budget.

- SG edge (4 x A100 equiv): colocate with SG latency-sensitive traffic; enable prefix cache (20% hit expected) to reduce cross-region calls.

- EU standby (2 x A100 equiv): warm failover and low-cost rerun lane for longer batch jobs.

SLA and exceptions: to meet your strict p99 target we should include a fallback policy: preferential routing to dedicated pools, with automatic model-variant fallback (smaller seq-length variant) if queue depth exceeds threshold. I attached a short SLA exception request draft for the legal team to review if we include cross-region failover guarantees.

Attachments: redwood_pool_mapping_v1.xlsx, pool_plan_apac_us_eu.md, sla_exception_request.docx

Soojin
Capacity Planning Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Rivera <ethan.rivera@swanlake.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@swanlake.ai, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request - US + APAC (pilot)

Ethan — thanks for the quick turnaround on the profiles. We reviewed and have a recommended plan and next steps: 

Recommended pilot offer (summary):
- Reserved baseline: US-West (8 x A100 equiv), SG edge (4 x A100 equiv), EU warm (2 x A100 equiv)
- Hybrid burst: dedicated baseline + controlled burst onto shared fleet for extreme tails (we’ll cap shared-fleet usage and alert on cross-over)
- Latency: with the proposed mapping and quantization path we expect p99 ~160-190ms for your median workload; we’ll run a validation eval against your dev dataset to confirm.
- Commitment term & pricing: 6-month reserved commitment; we can offer a trial discount of 20% off list for the initial term.

Next steps we propose: 
1) Redwood will share a draft SOW & mutual action plan (Google Doc) by EOD Monday.
2) We’ll run an eval job against your sample dataset to validate quantization quality and finalize the GPU mix (2 business days after we receive the signed intake form).
3) Procurement: I’ve attached a DocuSign powerform link for a non-binding MOU to start internal approvals.

Links: Mutual action plan: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1qX_Swanlake-MAP
DocuSign (trial MOU): https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd1234

If this looks good, Ethan — can we schedule a 30-minute kickoff next week (I’m flexible Tue/Wed)? Procurement — please confirm if you need any specific legal language for SLAs; we’ll include a redline-ready SOW.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
